protocol_checks.vulnerability_mechanism: PASS: Real SSRF bypass in is_url_safe. Source is attacker-controlled URL; sink is pre-parse u = remove_at_symbol_in_string(u) then new URL(u) / is_hostname_resolve_to_internal_ip(parsed.hostname). remove_at_symbol_in_string is s.replace(/@/g, ""), which deletes the userinfo/host delimiter so validation inspects a fabricated host while an HTTP client using the original URL still uses userinfo. Working vector on Node WHATWG: http://2@10.0.0.1/ parses as hostname 10.0.0.1 username 2, but after @-deletion becomes http://210.0.0.1/ (public 210.0.0.1). is_url_safe try/catch returns false only on parse failure, so concatenative userinfo+IP payloads return true. Same pre-parse deletion is also in is_redirect_safe. GHSA-cg4g-m8jx-vjv2 (withdrawn_at null) and CVE-2026-54722 (CVE.org state PUBLISHED, NVD vulnStatus Received, not rejected) describe this mechanism. CWE-76.

findings: Confirmed real vulnerability: is_url_safe (and is_redirect_safe) strip every '@' from the raw URL before WHATWG parsing, so userinfo-based hosts are not the hosts that get internal-IP checks. Concatenative payload http://2@10.0.0.1/ is a working bypass (validator sees 210.0.0.1; client uses 10.0.0.1). CVE-2026-54722 is PUBLISHED, GHSA-cg4g-m8jx-vjv2 is not withdrawn.
